invariants: Every new or changed English string gets a Welsh draft beside it in the same change, as the service's other copy does.

Every changed page works fully without JavaScript: every state change is a form post, every search and filter a form with a button that submits it, and JavaScript only enhances a page that already works (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 6; conflicts:c-006).

A behaviour is built with GOV.UK Frontend first, then another tested government library (Ministry of Justice, HMRC, Scottish Government); no custom JavaScript is written to copy the prototype, pop-ups are not built and confirmations stay pages (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 5, 7 and 19).
Pages are built from GOV.UK Frontend components and govuk-* classes; the prototype's custom app-dr2-* blocks are not copied.

A search box is the real frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select and behaves as the real frontend configures it; its entries are what MDM serves through reference-data, and only how the list reads follows the prototype (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 1 to 4).

Where a row changes a page or behaviour the high-risk plants frontend also has, the same increment changes plants too: plants mirrors the structure, wording patterns, components and behaviour, and keeps its own questions, data and step order (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 43 and 44).
Shared wording in a frontend's shared copy is never reworded in place; a set-specific string goes in the feature's own copy (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 41).

Notification statuses are only ever added, never renamed or removed, and each new status is mapped in every frontend that reads it before the animals backend first sends it (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 42).
A page in its error state keeps the 'Error: ' prefix on its browser title (conflicts:c-006).
'Save and return to overview' saves without the page's required-answer checks, but still refuses an answer that fails its own format rule (conflicts:c-211; ruling:sam-2026-10-07).
Notifications, templates and address book entries stay scoped to the signed-in user's organisation (or user, for templates); nothing lists another organisation's records.
Each increment updates the tests repo's specs, page objects and journey helpers its change breaks, in the same change.

increments.title: Germinal Commodity details asks total gross weight, number of packages and temperature, and the backend stores and publishes them with interim typeCodes
increments.detail: The germinal set's copy of Commodity details asks, for each chosen species, an optional 'Total gross weight' in kilograms and a 'Number of packages', and always asks one optional 'Temperature' for the consignment. A germinal commodity has one Selected commodities row. The animals backend stores the gross weight as a decimal on each species line and the temperature on every line, and shows them back; neither is published, because the current PIMS profile (gbn-ag-pims v0.2.0) has no field for them. The number of packages is the line's quantity on GBN-AG. Until the germinal catalogue separates embryos from ova, each germinal trade line carries an interim typeCode: SEMEN for a semen line and EMBRYO for a combined 'Embryos/Ova' line. The germinal set always asks the consignment's temperature; the animals backend stores it on the record and shows it back, but never publishes it, because the current PIMS profile (gbn-ag-pims v0.2.0) has no field for it. A germinal products notification is published on the same GBN-AG events and payload as a live-animals one, carrying only what that profile already carries and leaving out the sections the germinal set never asks (unweaned animals, CPH number, per-animal permanent address), as the mapper already leaves out an unanswered section. No PIMS profile, trade-imports-schemas data shape or trade-imports-dynamics-gateway mapping changes; the PIMS schema update for germinal products is EUDPA-686, outside this backlog. Once germinal lines carry their own typeCode, every live-animal trade line carries typeCode LIVE_ANIMAL too.
acceptanceCriteria: Each germinal species block asks 'Total gross weight' in a narrow text input with the suffix 'kg', before 'Number of packages'; left blank it shows no error. increments.title: Upload documents remembers where the trader came from and returns them there

increments.title: Save and continue no longer waits for virus scans, and Save and return to overview keeps a typed-in document
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 saves a complete document and moves the trader on at once when they press Save and continue, even while a document is still being scanned, and applies the same check before Save and return to overview, saving a document whose type is chosen. Today Save and continue saves the document and brings the trader back to the page, any document not yet scanned clean holds them, and Save and return to overview leaves at once and drops a part-filled document. Waiting for the scan is not a constraint, because the backend only publishes documents that scanned clean, so pending scans stop holding the trader; a document the scan rejected still does.

increments.title: Germinal identification asks once per species for donor, dates and identification number, and the backend stores them unpublished

Valid germinal Commodity details continue to this page. The germinal products set's own copy of Identification details counts packages, not animals: its Selected commodities quantity column reads 'Number of packages' and shows each species' saved number of packages, where the live-animals page shows Number of animals. This is the one germinal requirement on this page's summary that the animal-identification area holds; the germinal-products area holds the rest of the germinal identification page. The germinal set collects a donor name or ID, a collection date, a production date and an identification mark for each germinal species. The PIMS profile has no field for them, so the animals backend is their only home: it stores them, the service shows them back, and the GBN-AG payload carries none of them. Each date is a date-only YYYY-MM-DD value. Where they sit on the record (on the per-item identifier entries of each line, as animal identifiers do, or on the species line) is decided in the build from the real model, not the prototype's shape.

increments.title: A permanent address page for cats and dogs, with one card per animal and a same-as-destination choice
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks for each pet's permanent address on its own page in the consignment parties section, opened from the consignment addresses page, instead of inside the animal identification form. Cats, dogs and ferrets need one; other live mammals, which share their commodity code 01061900, do not. It is built now for cats and dogs over today's catalogue, and the same rule takes in ferrets once the catalogue holds them. The page has a card for each animal that needs one, showing the identifiers already given, and asks for each whether the animal lives at the place of destination or at a new address, revealing the address fields only when a new address is chosen. Each animal's choice and address are stored with the notification, every field in its own place, and a trader can save what they know and come back.

increments.title: The address book record carries the address's type and what it can be used for
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks what type of address is being added and what it can be used for, and Sam's 9 October ruling keeps both answers because a question the service asks must persist and DR1 asked for address pickers filtered by role (c-176). Today the address-book record is untyped and its API carries no type or use, so nothing can keep those answers, and the address book list's type tabs and the DR1 role-filtered pickers have nothing to filter on. Afterwards an API caller can create, read and update an address with its type and uses, in a field shape the address-book service designs in its own conventions, and addresses saved before the change still read back.
acceptanceCriteria: Creating an address through the address book API with its address type and one or more uses (place of origin, consignor, place of destination, consignee, importer, branch address) stores them, and reading the address back by id returns the same type and the same uses (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-079; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-081; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-137; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-115, p1-116)
Updating an address through the API with a different set of uses replaces its uses with the new set, and the read-back shows the new set (repo:addressbook p2-071; prototype:dr2-1-source p16-079)

A create or update carrying a use outside those six is refused with a 400 validation problem whose errors name the uses, and nothing is saved (repo:addressbook p1-039, p1-045; ruling:sam-2026-10-07 p1-010)
An address created without a type or uses, and every address saved before this change, is still accepted and reads back with no type and no uses (repo:addressbook p1-001, p1-003)

The address book's locked API contract describes the type and uses on the create and update requests and on the read response, with the six allowed uses (repo:addressbook p2-097, p2-098; document:dr1-parity-backlog p7-064, p7-065)
notes: Unchanged by the 9 October afternoon and templates rulings; the re-distil only renumbered claim references. Pass 1 slice on its own: the typed record is the foundation the add form's uses question, the list's type tabs (address-book-list area) and DR1's role-filtered pickers rest on, so it lands first and gates. Observable through the API in every environment the tests repo's address book API client reaches (local stack and CDP). The field names and shape are the address-book service's (c-176; ruling 9 October claims 66, 70, 116), so no criterion names the prototype's 'primary type' or 'address book type'. Type and uses stay optional on the API so a journey's handshake add and every existing record keep saving; the add form makes a use required outside a journey. Updates fully replace the editable fields, so the edit page must post the stored type and uses back; that is the edit row's criterion. Decision kept: refuse an unknown use with a 400 (validation clause of ruling:sam-2026-10-07).
increments.gate: Check the type and uses field names, the six use values and how a record without them reads back in the locked contract, before the add form, the address book list's type tabs and the DR1 address pickers build on it.

increments.title: Adding an address starts by choosing its type
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks what kind of address is being added before any fields, because the type decides the form and the uses offered next. Today the address book's add is the address form itself. Afterwards 'Add a new address' on the address book opens a new 'Choose an address type' page, on a path of its own in the INS front door's path shape, offering three types: 'Origin or Consignor', 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch'. 'Transporter' is left out until transporter management is decided (ruling 9 October pm, c-306). Choosing a type moves on to the address form, which stays where it is today (the page the animals frontend's handshake links to), retitled 'Add address and contact details' and able to go back to the type page. The chosen type is remembered while the add is in progress and cleared when it starts afresh or saves. The address types offered when adding an address read as Design Release 2.1 has them, each with its hint, in order, with Branch Address after a divider. Transporter is left out until transporter management is decided. This is the add-and-edit area's 'Choose an address type' step; the requirement came to this area because its claims sit beside the list's type labels, so the combiner merges it into that row.
acceptanceCriteria: From the address book list, 'Add a new address' opens a page with the caption 'Add a new address', the heading 'Choose an address type', a radio group whose legend repeats the heading visually hidden, and a 'Back' link to the address book list (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-001, p16-003, p16-004, p16-005, p16-013; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-038, p16-039; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-104, p6-105, p6-106, p6-112)

increments.title: View and delete pages return the user to where they opened the address from, including an animals journey page

increments.title: Address book list split into three category tabs with a Type column

An address shows on every tab whose category holds one of its types, so the address book API learns to return one category's addresses. The tables gain a Type column with the address's type labels. The INS frontend adds the MoJ frontend package at the animals frontend's major version. The tests repo's shared address book fixtures carry a type so they land on the right tab and the journeys still find them, and the k6 performance suite's address book scenarios search and count per tab. The Transporter tab waits with transporter management.
acceptanceCriteria: The list shows three tabs in this order: 'Origin and Consignor', 'Destination, Consignee and Importer' and 'Branch', drawn as the Ministry of Justice sub navigation; each is a link that loads the address book list on that tab, with JavaScript on or off, and the selected one is marked. increments.title: Search the whole row, 8 addresses a page, a list that clamps stale page numbers and a stub that behaves like the real book
increments.detail: Search finds an address by anything the row shows: name, type labels, every address line and country, not only name, town and postcode. The list pages at 8 through the address book service's server-side page size setting. The filter stays a GET form that the search button or Enter submits, working fully without JavaScript, and nothing re-requests the list as the user types. A stale page number shows a real page. The INS frontend's in-memory stub behaves the same, so the fit suite exercises the Design Release 2.1 list, and the E2E specs walk the address book through its own links.
acceptanceCriteria: Search matches the trimmed text, ignoring case and anywhere inside a word, against an address's name, type labels, address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county, postcode and country name, so 'ballymore' finds an address whose line 2 is 'Ballymore Road' and 'france' finds the addresses in France; a blank search is no search. increments.title: Saving a new address with its uses
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks what an address can be used for on the add-details step and saves the ticked uses with it, then shows the user the new address among its kind. Afterwards an Origin or Consignor address offers 'Place of origin' and 'Consignor' after a section break, a use is required once the fields are valid, the save stores the address's type and ticked uses in the address book, and the user lands on the address book list showing that type, with the new address first, a reworded success banner, its full address and searchable by its uses. The k6 performance suite's address-book scenarios follow the new add.
acceptanceCriteria: For 'Origin or Consignor' the address and contact fields show straight away with no address search, then a section break, then the uses question with the legend 'What can this address be used for?', the hint 'Select where this address can be used' and the checkboxes 'Place of origin' and 'Consignor', with no hint on either option (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-025, p16-048, p16-052, p16-053, p16-054, p16-055; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-054, p16-065, p16-066; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-119, p6-120)

increments.title: Choosing Transporter when adding to the address book hands over to adding a transporter

The Transporter option and its hand-over stay in the backlog, blocked, and the transporter area is re-distilled once it is decided (c-306). Design Release 2.1 lets a trader add a transporter from the address book: the add-a-transporter pages then lead back to the address book rather than to a notification. This draft covers the transporter pages' side of that route: the Back link, the cancel button and where a save lands when the add began in the address book, with the new transporter held as the organisation's. Blocked: the address book's transporter rows wait on transporter requirements. Once transporter management is decided and the address book manages transporters, the address types offered when adding an address include 'Transporter', after 'Place of Destination' and before the divider. Blocked with the rest of transporter management; the combiner merges it into the existing hand-over-to-adding-a-transporter row.

(prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p7-110, -p7-111)

increments.title: A notification journey's add opens Design Release 2.1's add page in journey mode, and saving or cancelling lands where Design Release 2.1 says
increments.detail: A trader adding an address from a notification's party picker keeps today's handshake to the INS address book (c-106), because which service serves the add page and writes the address book is cross-service behaviour the prototype cannot express. Reached that way, the INS add page skips 'Choose an address type', opens 'Add address and contact details' for the type the role implies with the role counted as the address's use, and offers Design Release 2.1's Back link and three actions. 'Save and select' saves the address and commits its copy for the role, landing on the Consignment addresses page; 'Save and return to address page' saves it and lands on the role's picker with the new address listed first; 'Cancel and return to hub' saves nothing. After either save the landing page shows a success banner that stays until the trader leaves or reloads (the INS script that hides it on a timer goes: WCAG 2.2.1). The round trip is proven from all five pickers. Observable on the compose stack and in CDP, where both frontends run; in the animals frontend's stub mode the pickers show no add link (c-106), so that environment is not named. A trader adding an address from a notification's party picker keeps today's handshake to the INS address book (c-106), because which service serves the add page and writes the address book is cross-service behaviour the prototype cannot express. Reached that way, the INS add page shows Design Release 2.1's add-address page in journey mode: it skips 'Choose an address type', opens 'Add address and contact details' for the type the role implies with the role's use ticked, and returns through the journey's address-return to the page each button names. Observable on the compose stack and in CDP, where both frontends run; in the animals frontend's stub mode the pickers show no add link (c-106).
acceptanceCriteria: Reached from a notification journey, the INS add page does not ask 'Choose an address type' and opens 'Add address and contact details' for the type the role implies, with that role already counted as the address's use (document:dr1-parity-backlog p7-007; prototype:dr2-1-source p8-092; trace:e2e p9-055; repo:tests p5-027; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-090; conflicts:c-106)
The add page has a 'Back' link that returns to the picker of the role the address is being added for (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-080; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-025; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-065)
The primary button reads 'Save and select' (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-109; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-023; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-064)

'Save and select' saves the address to the address book, puts a copy on the notification for the role, and lands on the Consignment addresses page, where that role shows the address with a 'Change' link (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-110; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-054, p7-055, p7-059; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-076; trace:e2e p9-070 to p9-073)

A secondary 'Save and return to address page' button saves the address to the address book without selecting it and lands on the role's picker, where the new address is listed first and no address is selected for the role (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-111; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-039, p7-041, p7-060; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-068; trace:e2e p8-093, p8-094, p9-074)

After either save the landing page shows a GOV.UK notification banner titled 'Success' reading '<Name> address added to your address book', which is still on screen however long the trader stays and goes only when they leave or reload the page (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-040, p7-055; document:dr1-parity-backlog p7-008; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p1-096, p1-097)

The page offers a 'Cancel and return to hub' link that lands on the notification's hub and saves nothing to the address book or the notification (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-109; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-024, p7-064; trace:e2e p9-075, p9-076)

The end-to-end suite drives 'Save and select', 'Save and return to address page' and 'Cancel and return to hub' from each of the five role pickers (place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination), on the compose stack and in CDP (repo:tests p5-032, p5-033; trace:e2e p9-077; repo:frontend p9-195)
The journey's address-return still refuses an unknown fulfilment or a stale handshake token, for each of the new landings (repo:frontend p9-139, p9-141; conflicts:c-106)

On the compose stack and in CDP, 'Add a new address' on a notification's party page still hands over to the INS address book's add page through today's handshake, only for a registered journey, with the return built on the server (repo:insfrontend p3-095 to p3-107; trace:e2e p15-006, p15-007; c-106)

Reached by the handshake, the INS add page does not ask 'Choose an address type' and opens 'Add address and contact details' for the type the role implies, with that role's use ticked (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-088, p16-091; c-106)

'Save and select' saves the address and commits its copy to the notification for the role, landing on the Consignment addresses page; 'Save and return to address page' saves it and lands on the role's picker with nothing selected; 'Cancel and return to hub' saves nothing; each lands through the journey's address-return (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-088 to p16-095; repo:tests p5-034 to p5-036; c-106)

Landing back in the journey shows the journey page's own banner and not the INS address book's banner, and the journey still refuses a return with an unknown fulfilment or a stale handshake token (repo:insfrontend p3-108 to p3-112, p3-138; trace:e2e p15-008, p15-009)
notes: Combines the drafts of the party-address-add-and-edit, address-book-add-and-edit areas for this row: they change the same pages and record, so building them apart would repeat the same set-up, review and ladder.

Combines the journey-mode type skip (req-1958, now this area's), the buttons-and-copy slice (Save and select, Save and return to address page, Cancel and return to hub, Back), the landing and banner slice and the every-picker proof: all change the one return contract between the INS add page and the journey's address-return, and the proof is of the same round trip. Combiner: the existing inc-080 also covers req-1284 (journey mode of the INS add page), which belongs to the address-book-add-and-edit area; this draft lists only this area's requirements and leaves out req-1284's criteria (the INS banner not shown on landing, the registered live-animals handshake). Merge the two drafts back into inc-080 as before, keeping its id and gate. repos is in merge order: frontend before insfrontend, because the journey's address-return must accept each new landing before the INS page sends it. The banner that stays (req-674) removes the INS script that hides it on a timer. The picker the second save lands on is the role-filtered picker the party picker area builds (inc-087, req-673 deltaNote); the address book already lists newest first, so 'listed first' is observable on today's picker and this row does not depend on inc-087, avoiding a dependency from the address-book theme back to consignment-parties. Depends on inc-077 (and through it the type-step and add-details rows). A germinal products notification uses the same handshake with its own INS return entry (req-1831), built in its own row.

Unchanged by the 9 October afternoon and templates rulings. This draft holds only this area's requirement (req-1284). Combiner: merge into inc-080 with the party-address-add-and-edit area's draft (req-637, req-671 to req-675, req-678, req-1958), as the backlog already does, keeping its id and gate: both change the one return contract between the INS add page and the journey's address-return. Observable on the compose stack and in CDP, where both frontends run; in the animals frontend's stub mode the pickers show no add link (c-106), so the fit suites do not observe the hand-over, and no criterion here claims them. repos lists frontend before insfrontend because the journey's address-return must accept each landing before the INS page sends it. Depends on the type-step, add-details and uses-and-save rows (the journey-mode page opens the add-details step with the role's use ticked) and, through inc-077, on the party-address area's pickers. A germinal products notification uses the same handshake with its own INS return entry (ruling 9 October claim 61), built by the germinal area's rows, not here.
increments.gate: Look at the changed handshake return before anything builds on it: each of the three actions and the Back link lands on the right journey page from all five pickers, and the address-return still refuses an unknown fulfilment or a stale token.

increments.title: Destination-side journey add pages find UK addresses by a search that works without JavaScript
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1's consignee, importer and place of destination add pages, reached from the journey through the INS frontend's address book (c-106), start with a UK address search, as the address book's own 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' step does. The 9 October afternoon ruling (c-287) has the version that works without JavaScript built: a search form submitted to the server by its Search button, results on the returned page, and a pick that fills the fields from the INS backend's address lookup (c-178). Sam's 9 October ruling blocks all of it in every environment until the address lookup becomes a real feature; until then the pages open on manual entry, and the area is re-distilled once the lookup lands (c-217).
acceptanceCriteria: The consignee, importer and place of destination add pages and the address book's 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' add-details step start with a text field labelled 'Search for an address', placeholder 'Start typing...', browser autocomplete turned off, and a search button whose accessible name is 'Search' (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-086; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-042, p7-043; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-069)
With JavaScript turned off, pressing 'Search' submits the search to the server and the returned page lists the matching UK addresses (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p1-046, p1-047; conflicts:c-287)

Submitting the search lists matching UK addresses from the address lookup under 'Address search results', each a choice showing the organisation name where the lookup has one and the lookup's full one-line address, and no Northern Ireland address (postcode starting 'BT') is offered (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-087; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-053, p7-063; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-073; conflicts:c-178)

Picking a result fills address line 1, address line 2, town or city and postcode with country United Kingdom, all editable, leaving the name for the trader where the lookup gives none and leaving email address and phone number empty; earlier error messages stay until the next submit (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-089; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-048 to p7-050, p7-048-m1, p7-052; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-074; conflicts:c-178)
Picking a result whose lookup address has a locality keeps the locality in the filled form, in address line 2 with the street (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-048-m2; conflicts:c-178)
openQuestions: Blocked (req-647, req-648, req-650, req-651 blockedBy; c-217): the INS backend's address lookup must become a real feature. Today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local on a standalone page and not wired in. Who: the team building the INS address lookup. Once it lands this area is re-distilled, which settles which environments the search runs in and what else it needs (ruling 2026-10-09 p1-178, p1-180).
notes: Unchanged from the last distil. The search is a server-submitted form that works without JavaScript (c-287). The JavaScript-only and design-dependent parts (req-649, req-652, req-653, req-654, req-1957) sit in their own waiting-on-design row. Built on the address book's own search row (inc-072, also blocked) and the manual-entry page of inc-078.

increments.title: The journey add page's Country select offers the countries reference-data serves from MDM
increments.detail: On the place of origin and consignor add pages the trader picks the address's country by hand. Sam's 9 October ruling takes the MDM block off this row (c-107): the select offers reference-data's unfiltered country list, which is what MDM serves, and no list is typed or edited in code. Where MDM's content differs from Design Release 2.1's 42 entries, such as the EU outermost regions and the Crown Dependencies, that is MDM's content to change. The stub tidy-up regenerates the local country fixture from MDM, so the names and counts the page's checks expect move to the recaptured fixture. The select stays a plain select, not the accessible autocomplete, because the prototype shows it as one; the INS address book's country autocomplete is a follow-on recorded in deferred.md (ruling 2026-10-09 pm). Observable in the INS frontend's fit suite, on the compose stack and in CDP.
acceptanceCriteria: On the place of origin and consignor add pages the Country select offers every country in reference-data's unfiltered country list for that environment, with the names it serves, and no country it does not serve (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-129, p1-132, p1-143; conflicts:c-107)

On the compose stack the select holds as many countries, with the same names, as the stub's regenerated MDM country fixture serves unfiltered, not today's 32 sovereign states (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-149, p1-162; trace:e2e p9-064)
The Country select is still a plain drop-down select, not a type-ahead autocomplete (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p1-023 to p1-025, p1-040, p1-041; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-061)

The end-to-end and fit checks of the select take their country names and counts from the captured reference-data fixture, and no country list is typed by hand in them (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-140, p1-141, p1-144)
notes: Adds one criterion over the last distil: req-644 now says the select stays a plain select and the INS address book's country autocomplete is a deferred follow-on (ruling 2026-10-09 pm), so that is checked. Kept apart from inc-078: it depends on the stub tidy-up row at the head of the reference-lists theme (inc-173), because ruling p1-149 has that row change the names and counts these checks assert, and on inc-078 (the origin-side page). The stub tidy-up owns regenerating the stub and capture fixtures; this row only aligns the add page and its checks. Today the INS select pins United Kingdom first and drops GB from the list; that ordering is not list content and is kept.

increments.title: Welsh for the redesigned address book list, view and delete pages
increments.detail: Every new or changed English string on the address book list, view and delete pages has a Welsh counterpart, marked as an unreviewed machine draft until it has Welsh Language Standards sign-off, so a Welsh user sees the same Design Release 2.1 page rather than today's. The Welsh for the Transporter tab waits with that tab.
acceptanceCriteria: With Welsh selected, the list, view and delete pages show a Welsh string for every piece of copy the Design Release 2.1 rows added or changed (intro, 'Filter addresses', 'Search', the placeholder, the three tab names and headings, column headers, Type labels and options, 'County (optional)', 'Delete this address?', 'Confirm that you want to delete this address.', 'This action cannot be undone.', 'Yes, delete', 'No, cancel', the banners and the page titles), and no English string is left. (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p2-098; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-045)

Today's Welsh strings for the replaced copy, such as 'Rheoli cyfeiriadau a ddefnyddir ar draws gwasanaethau mewnforio ac allforio.', 'Chwilio cyfeiriadau' and 'Dileu cyfeiriad', no longer show. (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p2-099 to repo-insfrontend-p2-105)
Each new Welsh string is visibly marked, where the Welsh copy is kept, as an unreviewed machine draft awaiting Welsh Language Standards sign-off. (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p2-098)

sources.ref: ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-045 (Welsh row no longer waits on the Transporter tab; its Welsh waits with that tab)

notes: A requirement sits in one row, and req-1186 spans the copy every other buildable row in this area changes, so it is the last of them and checks the whole set. Builders of the earlier rows add a Welsh machine draft beside each English string they add, so the Welsh page never falls back to English for long; this row completes and verifies it. ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-045 takes the dependency on the blocked Transporter-tab row away: the Welsh for the Transporter tab waits with that tab. Depends on every buildable row in this area: the list row (inc-063), the return-path row (inc-066, and through it the view and delete rows) and the search row (inc-069, and through it the tabs and Type-filter rows). Kept the existing row's id.

increments.title: Welsh drafts for the new add and edit copy
increments.detail: The address book keeps English and Welsh copy side by side. Changing only the English would leave the Welsh describing the old pages. Afterwards every new or changed English string on the add and edit pages built now has a Welsh entry, still marked as an unreviewed machine draft.
acceptanceCriteria: The address book's Welsh copy has an entry for every new or changed English string on 'Choose an address type', the add-details step (every type's layout, the uses question and every error message) and the edit page, and no add or edit page shows an English string where the Welsh copy is in use (repo:insfrontend p3-113 to p3-120)
The Welsh copy stays marked as an unreviewed machine draft that must not ship to users without Welsh Language Standards sign-off (repo:insfrontend p3-113)
notes: Unchanged by the 9 October afternoon and templates rulings. Depends on every todo row in this area that adds or changes English copy (validation messages, type step, add-details form, uses and save, manual entry for Destination and Branch, edit). It does not wait for the blocked rows (the address search rows and the Transporter hand-over); each drafts its own Welsh when it is built. Kept as one sweep so the Welsh is checked once against the finished English. The combiner may fold it into the address book list area's Welsh row, which edits the same copy file.

increments.title: Roles and addresses page: intro, warning, Consignor name, named add links and full addresses
increments.detail: Brings the live-animals roles and addresses page's words and rows in line with Design Release 2.1, inside the summary list DR1 kept (c-087). The page gains an intro paragraph. The fraud warning loses its full stop. The consignor party is called 'Consignor' rather than 'Consignor or exporter'. Every empty row offers a link that names what it adds instead of a bare 'Add'. An answered row shows the whole chosen address, not just the name, so a trader can check every address without opening each picker. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm carries the 'Consignor' rename to the high-risk plants frontend's consignor picker and its check-answers label in the same change, so the two services name the party the same way. Every new or changed string carries a Welsh machine draft.
acceptanceCriteria: Under the heading 'Consignment addresses' the page shows the paragraph 'Add all the addresses that are involved in the consignment.' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-004; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-004; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-004)

The warning reads 'Providing a false address is an act of fraud' with no closing full stop, and its Welsh text has no closing full stop either (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-005; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-005; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-036; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-030)

The consignor row is labelled 'Consignor', and the consignor picker's heading and page title say 'Consignor', in English and Welsh; 'Consignor or exporter' no longer appears on either page, and the consignor picker's address is unchanged (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-020, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-137; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-008, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-027; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-030; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-034, repo-frontend-p9-090)

In the high-risk plants frontend, the consignor picker's heading and page title say 'Consignor', and check your answers labels the consignor 'Consignor', in English and Welsh; 'Consignor or exporter' no longer appears on either page, and the consignor picker's address is unchanged (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-037; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-056, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-059, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-081)

Empty rows offer the links 'Add a place of origin', 'Add a consignor', 'Add a consignee', 'Add an importer' and 'Add a place of destination', each opening that party's picker (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-019, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-021, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-023, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-025, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-027; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-034)
An empty CPH number row offers the link 'Add a CPH number', opening the CPH number page (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-028; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-017)

An answered party row shows the name on its own line, then each address line on its own line, the last ending with a comma and the country name, such as 'Hull, HU9 5PX, United Kingdom' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-032; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-033; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-046; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-027)

With either frontend in Welsh, every string this change adds or alters shows a Welsh counterpart, still marked as an unreviewed machine draft (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-029, repo-frontend-p9-089, repo-frontend-p9-090; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-048-m1; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-031)
The roles and addresses page has no serious or critical accessibility violations (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-176)
notes: Re-drafted on this re-distil. The requirements behind it did not change in substance; the provenance now cites the renumbered afternoon ruling claim (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-037 for the plants Consignor rename) and the current plants claims (repo-plantsfrontend-p6-056, p6-059, p6-081). Combines four thin slices that all change the roles and addresses page's copy and rows: the intro and warning, the Consignor rename, the named add links and the full address on answered rows. Each repeats the same page, copy files and tests, so building them apart gains little. The plants rename rides along because req-564 puts it in the same increment. The summary list stays (c-087); the prototype's headed sections are set aside. c-103: the consignor's id, route and address-book role stay as they are in both frontends, and the animals overview task hint 'Consignor or Exporter, ...' stays. The plants overview hub copy that also names 'Consignor or exporter' is not named by req-564 and is left as it is. c-089: the visually hidden suffix on the add link goes, as the link now names the party. req-619 (Welsh for every new or changed string) sits here, and every other row of this area keeps the same rule. The tests repo's animals page object and flow that name 'Consignor or exporter' and the 'Add' link, and the plants consignor page object and review spec, change with it. The germinal-products set's copy of this page (req-1827) is taken after this row lands, so it inherits these changes. Theme: consignment-parties.

increments.title: Party picker layout: add button, search control, results heading and count, address lines and blank save
increments.detail: Brings the five live-animals party pickers' layout in line with Design Release 2.1. By ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm, the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers change with them. The search label is medium and the search runs from an icon button. A 'Select an address' heading and a reworded results count sit above the table. The table sits in one fieldset. Each address line takes its own line. Saving with nothing chosen is no longer an error. On the animals pickers 'Add a new address' becomes a secondary button beside the heading; the plants pickers, which offer no add control, stay without one. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm brings the high-risk plants consignment contact page into the party pickers' layout in the same increment as the animals and plants consignor and place of destination pickers: the same search control, the results count under the 'Select an address' heading, the radios in a fieldset with a hidden legend, and each address read back on separate lines. It keeps its search over the whole address book, its five-a-page pagination and its 'Selected address' inset.
acceptanceCriteria: On each of the five animals pickers on the compose stack, 'Add a new address' is a secondary button beside the picker's heading, and no 'Add a new address' link sits under the intro; in stub mode the pickers offer no add control (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-053; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-054; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-029; repo:tests repo-tests-p5-022, repo-tests-p5-024)

The high-risk plants consignor and place of destination pickers still offer no 'Add a new address' control (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-015; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-036)

On the animals pickers and the plants consignor and place of destination pickers, the search label 'Search' is styled as a medium heading (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-071; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-038; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-001)

On those pickers the search runs from a search icon button beside the box whose accessible name is 'Search'; there is no secondary 'Search' text button, and with JavaScript turned off pressing the icon button narrows the list on the server (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-071; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-053, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-054; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-035, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-038; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-003, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-004)

Under the search, each of those pickers shows the heading 'Select an address' above the results count (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-059; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-056; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-017; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-008)

The results count reads 'Showing <visible> out of <total> results' in English, with its Welsh counterpart, and changes when a search narrows the list, on the animals pickers and the plants consignor and place of destination pickers (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-059; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-036; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-018, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-019; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-008, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-049)

On those pickers the address table sits inside one fieldset whose legend 'Select an address' is read by a screen reader but not shown (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-057; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-020; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-010)

On those pickers the Address column shows each address line on its own line, with no commas joining them (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-060; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-066; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-011)

On an animals picker, pressing 'Save and continue' with no address chosen shows no error and returns to the roles and addresses page, the party still empty, or still holding the address it held before (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-072, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-073; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-078, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-103; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-055)

On the plants consignor or place of destination picker, pressing 'Save and continue' with no address chosen shows no error and moves on to the page that picker's save leads to, the party still empty or still holding its earlier address (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-039; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-032, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-034, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-075, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-086)

On both frontends, choosing an address that is not, or no longer, in the organisation's book is still refused with its party error (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-181; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-019, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-088)

Every new or changed string has a Welsh machine-draft counterpart, and every changed picker has no serious or critical accessibility violations (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-089, repo-frontend-p9-188; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-049, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-078, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-087)

The high-risk plants consignment contact page takes the same picker layout: the search control in place of its 'Search' label, 'Name, address or country' hint and secondary 'Search' button; the results count under the 'Select an address' heading instead of in the table caption; the radios in a fieldset with a hidden legend; and each address read back on separate lines, with the country no longer in a column of its own (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p3-038; repo:plantsfrontend p7-052, p7-056, p7-057, p7-059, p7-089)

The high-risk plants consignment contact picker keeps its five-a-page pagination and 'Selected address' inset, following the default of c-292 (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p3-038; repo:plantsfrontend p7-062, p7-070)

With the Welsh language chosen, every new or changed string on the plants contact page shows in Welsh, marked as a machine draft that must not ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off, and the page has no serious or critical accessibility violations (repo:plantsfrontend p7-090, p7-091)

notes: Combines the drafts of the consignment-parties, cph-permanent-and-contact areas for this row: they change the same pages and record, so building them apart would repeat the same set-up, review and ladder.

Re-drafted on this re-distil; no requirement behind it changed in substance. Provenance now cites the renumbered afternoon ruling claims (p1-035 every search a form with a submitting button, p3-015 no plants equivalent leaves plants alone, p3-038 plants picker layout, p3-039 plants lenient blank save) and the current plants claims. The pickers keep 'Save and continue' alone (c-099). The tests repo's animals e2e tests and the plants parties and destination specs that expect the 'Select a <party> from the list' error on a blank save and the comma-joined address change with it. req-1965 (the plants contact page's pagination and inset) is a question, not adopted, so it is not built; c-292's default keeps today's behaviour.

increments.title: Role-filtered party pickers on one page
increments.detail: Gives every address-book record one or more roles, and makes each live-animals party picker, and the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers, offer only the organisation's addresses for its role, all on one page. The address book stores the roles and lists one role's addresses unpaginated; each frontend asks for its picker's role. Records saved before roles existed are offered on every picker until given a role, so nobody loses an address on a guess. Stub mode in both frontends gets roles on its canned records, so it filters too. Because each page is now one role's addresses, pagination and the 'Selected address' inset go. Search stays the server search behind the submitting search button; filtering as the trader types waits on design in its own row.
acceptanceCriteria: On the compose stack, an address saved with only the consignee role appears on the consignee picker and not on the place of origin, consignor, importer or place of destination pickers (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-063; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-070, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-098; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-047)

An address saved with the exporter role appears on the consignor picker; there is no separate exporter picker (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-064, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-137; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116)
An address saved with several roles appears on the picker of every party whose role it carries (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-065)

On the compose stack, the high-risk plants consignor picker offers only addresses carrying the consignor role and the plants place of destination picker only those carrying the place of destination role, each with the role-less records too (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-040; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-006)

An address-book record with no role appears on all five animals pickers and on both plants pickers, on the compose stack and in CDP (document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-051; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-040)

The address book returns an organisation's addresses for one requested role in a single unpaginated list, carrying each record's roles, and never returns a deleted record (document:dr1-parity-notes document-dr1-parity-notes-p1-022, document-dr1-parity-notes-p1-023; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-050, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-052; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-115)

In stub mode, each animals picker and each plants picker lists only the canned records that carry its role (with any canned record that has no role), so the pickers do not all list the same addresses (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-168, repo-frontend-p9-169, repo-frontend-p9-170; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-092)

Each animals picker and each plants picker lists every address it offers on one page, with no page-number links and no Previous or Next links, however many addresses the role has (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-063; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-052, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-056, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-057; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-041; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-007, repo-plantsfrontend-p6-021)

No animals or plants picker shows a 'Selected address:' inset; a party's chosen address shows as its checked row when the picker is reopened (document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-050, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-055; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-041; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-017)

Submitting a search still narrows the one-page list on the server in both frontends (document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-054; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-066)
notes: Re-drafted on this re-distil; no requirement behind it changed in substance. Provenance now cites the renumbered afternoon ruling claims (p1-066 builds inc-087 now, p3-040 and p3-041 the plants half) and the templates ruling's same-time rule (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-templates-p1-044), which req-594 now cites. Combines role filtering (address-book roles and a role-scoped list, each frontend asking by role, the role-less fallback, stub roles) with one-page listing and dropping the 'Selected address' inset, because c-094 rules they land together: one page is only sensible once it is one role's addresses, and the inset only existed to carry a selection across pages. req-592 (filtering as the trader types) stays out: it is blocked on design question 5, in its own row. c-100: DR1's typed-record block is lifted; the typed record is built in trade-imports-address-book. Its field shape for roles is the address book's own design (req-611, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116). The record's type and uses are inc-059's, in the address-book theme, which this row depends on; the role-scoped list sits in the address book's service code, and the record shape in its address package is shared with that theme. c-101: role-less records show on every picker until given a role, in the compose stack and CDP alike, never filtered on a guess; in CDP every record saved before this lands has no role, so the criterion is observable there. Both frontends' address-book services stay read-only (c-106, req-618). Giving a record its roles through the INS address book's add and edit pages belongs to the address-book-add-and-edit and party-address-add-and-edit areas; on the compose stack the role-carrying records these criteria use are set-up for a one-page assertion through the address book, which the test rules allow. The picker's search must still answer a 255-character term (req-1828, exists, driven by the k6 scripts). The animals stub book mirrors the tests repo's address-book fixture record for record, so both gain roles together. The tests repo's pagination and later-page-selection tests (repo-tests-p5-013, p5-018, p5-020) and the plants picker specs change with it. Theme: consignment-parties.
increments.gate: Look at role filtering on the compose stack and in stub mode, in both frontends, before the rows that rest on it build: a role-carrying record appears only on its roles' pickers, a record with no role appears on every picker, the list is one page, and the server search narrows it. The same-as row, the place of origin country search, the live filter row and the germinal set's copy of the pickers build on this.

increments.title: Same-as shortcuts on the roles and addresses page
increments.detail: Lets a trader fill the consignor from the place of origin, and the importer and place of destination from the consignee, with one button press on the live-animals roles and addresses page, as Design Release 2.1 draws. The button copies the source party's record onto the notification as an independent copy, so a later change to the source does not ripple through.
acceptanceCriteria: With a place of origin chosen and no consignor, the Consignor row shows a 'Same as place of origin' button styled as a link beside 'Add a consignor' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-033; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-042; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-049)

With a consignee chosen and no importer, the Importer row shows a 'Same as consignee' button styled as a link beside 'Add an importer'; with a consignee chosen and no place of destination, the Place of destination row shows a 'Same as consignee' button beside 'Add a place of destination' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-034; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-043, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-044; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-050)

No same-as button shows while its source party is empty or its target party already has an address, and no other pair of parties offers one (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-049, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-050; prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-038; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-020)

Pressing a same-as button reloads the roles and addresses page with no success banner, the target row showing the source party's name and full address with a 'Change' link and no same-as button (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-035, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-036; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-045, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-046, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-047, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-048; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-051)

After copying, changing the source party to a different address leaves the copied target party's address as it was (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-037; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-052; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-021)

The copy is made even when the source address does not carry the target party's role, and the target party then shows that address (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-037; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-099)

The copied party carries the source's name, address lines, country and contact details through to check your answers (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-036; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-085, repo-frontend-p9-086)

The same-as buttons work with JavaScript turned off, and every new string has a Welsh machine-draft counterpart (document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-023; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-089)
notes: Unchanged from the existing row: no requirement behind it moved. Combines the three same-as buttons and their shared show and copy rules: one page form, one copy behaviour, one set of tests. c-100: DR1's collision block does not hold this back. Today the summary list sits outside the page's form (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-023), so the buttons need the form around them. The prototype's same-as-<source>:<role> action value is not adopted (req-1829, out of scope): the button posts the real service's own fields. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm leaves plants unchanged here: plants has no roles and addresses page to carry the shortcut (p3-015). Order: build after the roles and addresses page copy row (it asserts the full address and the named add links) and after the role-filtered pickers row (the 'copy even when the target's picker would not offer it' criterion needs role-carrying records). On the compose stack the role-carrying record for that criterion is set-up for a one-page assertion, allowed by the test rules. Theme: consignment-parties.

increments.title: Place of origin picker searches by country
increments.detail: Gives the live-animals place of origin picker the country search Design Release 2.1 draws, built as ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm directs. It has its own label, hint and placeholder. The search is the real frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select of the countries MDM serves through reference-data, with a button that submits the chosen country so the server keeps only the addresses in that country. Without JavaScript the native select and the button do the same. Filtering as the trader types waits on design and is not part of this row.
acceptanceCriteria: The place of origin picker's search is labelled 'Enter a country' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-054; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-072; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-035)

Its hint reads 'Enter each country that the consignment will travel through' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-054; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-127, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-103)

With JavaScript, its search box shows the placeholder 'Search for a country' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-054; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-072; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-010)

With JavaScript, the country search is an autocomplete offering the countries the service's country list holds, behaving as the frontend's other country autocompletes do (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-079-m1; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-005, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-006, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-008, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-009)

Choosing a country and pressing the search button reloads the picker showing only the addresses in that country, with the results count to match; pressing it with no country chosen shows every address (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-035, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-069; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-054)

With JavaScript turned off, the picker shows a select of the same countries, and choosing one and pressing the search button narrows the list in the same way (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-007, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-044; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-054)
The other four pickers keep their 'Search' label and free-text search, and every new string has a Welsh machine-draft counterpart (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-053, repo-frontend-p9-089)
The place of origin picker has no serious or critical accessibility violations with the country search in place (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-188)
notes: Re-drafted on this re-distil; no requirement behind it changed in substance. Provenance now cites the renumbered afternoon ruling claims: p1-005 to p1-009 (the frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select, MDM's entries, the component's own mechanics), p1-010 (label, hint and placeholder follow the prototype), p1-035 (every search a form with a submitting button), p1-044 and p1-069 (the no-JavaScript half is built now), p1-020 and p1-022 (the search box's look and wider rollout are EUDPA-635's). c-102: the prototype's own country widget, its as-you-type row filtering and its custom announcements are set aside; the as-you-type country filter waits on design as req-1951, in its own row. The placeholder is built now, which only the autocomplete can show. Combines the place of origin picker's label, hint, placeholder and country search: one picker, one search control. The search keeps the real service's field name and action (req-1829 out of scope, req-1828 exists); the native select may need a country value alongside the free-text q the k6 scripts drive, which the plan stage settles without breaking req-1828. The country list comes from the frontend's existing countries service (reference-lists theme); the accessible autocomplete component is the journey foundation's, used here, not changed. The plants frontend has no place of origin picker, so plants is unchanged (p3-015). Order: build after the role-filtered pickers row, whose one-page list this narrows, and after the picker layout row, which reshapes the search control. Theme: consignment-parties.

increments.title: Picker 'View' link to the INS address book and back
increments.detail: Replaces each live-animals picker row's in-place 'View details' expander with a 'View' link that opens the address in the INS address book, and makes the INS address book bring the trader back to the same picker. The INS frontend stays the one place an address is shown in full. The high-risk plants pickers are not wired to the INS address book and keep their 'View details' disclosure. DR1 asked for a way to correct a wrong saved address from the picker. Each live-animals picker row links to that saved address's own record in the INS address book, carrying the picker as its return, so the trader can correct or delete the record and come back to the picker they left. The INS frontend is the address book's only writer (c-106), so the record and its edit live there. Plants is not wired to the INS address book and takes none of it (ruling 2026-10-09 pm). Observable on the compose stack and in CDP; in stub mode the fit suite sees only the link.
acceptanceCriteria: Each animals picker row ends with a 'View' link, and there is no 'View details' expander (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-062; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-060)

On the compose stack, following 'View' opens that address in the INS address book, and its back control returns the trader to the same party picker of the same notification (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-061; prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-062)

The high-risk plants consignor and place of destination pickers keep their 'View details' disclosure and offer no 'View' link (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-064; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-012)
The 'View' link has a Welsh machine-draft counterpart (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-089)

Each party picker row offers a link to that saved address's own record in the INS address book which carries the picker as its return, so after correcting or deleting the record the trader comes back to the picker they left; if the row keeps an in-place 'View details', it no longer repeats the name, address lines and country the row's columns already show (document:dr1-parity-backlog p7-036, p7-042; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p3-048, p3-064; conflicts:c-106)
notes: Combines the drafts of the consignment-parties, party-address-add-and-edit areas for this row: they change the same pages and record, so building them apart would repeat the same set-up, review and ladder.

Re-drafted on this re-distil; req-601 is unchanged in substance, and its plants exclusion now cites the renumbered afternoon ruling claim ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-064. The plants criterion is a guard that the plants pickers are left alone; it touches no plants code, so plantsfrontend is not in repos. Kept apart: it is the area's only change to the INS frontend and carries a cross-service return path the others do not. c-097: the prototype wins; the INS frontend must honour the return path, and the tests repo's in-place expander test (repo-tests-p5-014) changes with it. In stub mode, where no INS frontend runs, the fit suite observes the link's presence only; where it leads is observed on the compose stack. The builder should accept only a return path inside the animals journey, as the INS add handshake already does (journey-registry), so the link is no open redirect; this is a safeguard, not a source requirement, so it is left out of the criteria. The return to a germinal products picker is req-1831's concern, not this row's. The existing row inc-090 also holds req-1960 (each picker row links to its record in the INS address book and back), another area's; this draft leaves it and its criterion for the combiner to carry over. Theme: consignment-parties.

Combiner: req-1960 is the same change as the party picker area's inc-090 'View' link (req-601), so merge this draft into inc-090 as the backlog already does, keeping its id. Whether the in-place 'View details' disclosure stays is the party picker area's call (req-601 drops it in favour of 'View'). Animals only.

increments.title: The CPH number page follows Design Release 2.1: who is asked, its help and hint, a blank save, and where it goes
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks for a county parish holding (CPH) number for every live animal kept on a holding. In the live-animals set every commodity but horses (0101) and the pet code 01061900 (cats, dogs, ferrets and other live mammals) gets the question, built now over the commodities today's catalogue holds, so the same rule takes in pigs, sheep, poultry and the rest once the MDM catalogue holds them with no further change. The page cannot be opened for a consignment it does not apply to. Its help gains a second place to find the number, the hint loses its punctuation, the boxes stop browsers offering saved values, and a trader can save the page blank and move on, with the gap held at submission instead. The page is a step of the consignment addresses section: opened from that page and always returning to it. The plants frontend has no CPH number and is not changed. Every changed English string gets its Welsh machine draft in the same change.
acceptanceCriteria: A live-animals consignment holding cattle or fish is asked for a CPH number, and its consignment addresses page has a CPH section; one holding only horses, cats or dogs is not asked and its consignment addresses page has no CPH section (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-001, p9-002; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-106; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-110; trace:e2e p6-068, p6-070; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-025, p1-057; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p2-014, p2-025; p3-022)
Opening the CPH number page for a consignment the question does not apply to sends the trader to the consignment addresses page (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-001; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-106)

The CPH help's second paragraph reads 'You can find your CPH number on documents from the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) or by checking your holding details on GOV.UK.', with 'checking your holding details on GOV.UK' a link to https://www.gov.uk/guidance/get-a-county-parish-holding-cph-number (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-009; trace:animals-fit p13-018; trace:e2e p6-084)

The CPH question's hint reads 'For example 12/345/6789', with no comma and no full stop, and still describes the whole group of three boxes (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-010; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-119; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-040; trace:animals-fit p13-007)
Each of the three CPH boxes turns browser autocomplete off and carries the pattern [0-9]* alongside the numeric input mode (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-012; trace:animals-fit p13-014)

Saving the CPH page with all three boxes empty shows no error: any saved CPH number is cleared, the trader returns to the consignment addresses page, the CPH section there stays incomplete, and the notification cannot be submitted until a number is added (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-014, p9-015, p9-004, p8-135)

increments.title: The Overview for a germinal products notification, with Commodity details Complete on valid packages
increments.detail: Each germinal products notification gets its own Overview page in the germinal products set, a copy of the live-animals Overview taken once this programme has built it, plus the germinal differences. Germinal products are counted by packages and weight, not by animals, so 'Your commodities' shows a packages card and a 'Kilograms' card in place of the animals card, totalling the gross weight entered (c-022). Screen-reader users get the same named regions as on the live-animals Overview, with the weight card named 'Gross weight summary' (c-244). Ruling 2026-10-09 splits the Commodity details completeness rule per set: on the germinal-products set the task is Complete once every chosen species has a valid number of packages and any total gross weight entered is valid.
